answer: Switching events on the power line inject brief carrier impulses, so a claimant timestamps the next impulse burst and neighbouring meters must report the same burst within a few milliseconds. The impulses are irregular and logged by the utility after the fact, so the atlas of possible fake times shrinks to nothing; an invented pattern, however velvet its timing, still fails, and a commitment made before the log is published stops backdating, while the dawn check catches any burst claimed before it happened.
